prerequisites: It is recommended that students have acquired the knowledge covered in Mechanics and Strength of Materials.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and skills for the calculation, design, and testing of machines.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Understands the conditioning factors in mechanical design.
Is able to consider different types of variables in design.
Knows the various machine elements and understands their operation.
Is able to address the basic analysis of machine elements.

syllabus_topics: Materials in machines and their properties.
Calculation of actions and dimensioning of simple elements.
Design of elements applying strength and rigidity criteria.
Analysis of elements using SolidWorks Simulation. Design improvements.

assessment_methods.method: Problem exam - Part II (aspects from continuous evaluation activities)

assessment_rules: The final grade is the maximum of two calculations. Option 1: Sum of scores from the written exam (max 2 points), problem exam Part I (max 6 points), and problem exam Part II (max 2 points). Option 2: Sum of scores from the written exam (max 2 points), problem exam Part I (max 6 points), and a weighted sum of 0.5 times the continuous evaluation activities score (max 2 points) plus 0.5 times the problem exam Part II score (max 2 points). To pass the course, the final grade must be equal to or greater than 5 points. Students may be required to demonstrate authorship of their work in an oral interview; failure to do so will result in a zero grade for those activities.
